finding: Round 6's `by_severity` argument was taken, and the deliverable it created lives entirely inside a list item titled "An audit-side `nonblocking_open` on `--record` and `--status`" in a section titled Non-Goals. Counted against the file: the strings `--merge`, `by_severity` and `audit_merge` occur on lines 230-234 and nowhere else in 312 lines -- all four occurrences inside Non-Goal 6. Every other surface that decides what gets built disagrees with it. §1 sizes the release as "**One deliverable**" and enumerates §2's four parts ("its resolution, its fence, its validation and its documentation") -- no output key. §2, the section an implementer reads for scope, never names `--merge`. §5's eleven tests never name it, so the one new emitted key in the release has no failing arm; §5's closing paragraph, which exists to name untested things deliberately, says "`clean` is this release's only gated surface" and lists `role_streaks[].open` and `spec_coverage_clean_rounds` -- a new JSON key on `--merge` is neither tested nor named as untested. The AX consequence is specific rather than stylistic: a decomposer builds §5's tests and §2's scope, and Non-Goals is the list it reads to learn what NOT to build, so the key does not ship, `clean: true` under `blocking` stays unreadable, and Non-Goal 6's own closing sentence -- "an operator setting `blocking` reads the round files for what was suppressed" -- survives as the shipped behaviour while the paragraph above it says the fix is in scope. The item also asserts both halves at once: its bolded title defers the thing and its bolded body says "The breakdown is in scope and ships on `--merge`".
suggestion: Move the two scope sentences out of Non-Goal 6 into §2 as a named part of the deliverable -- `tp audit --merge`'s summary gains `by_severity`, a count of non-`PASS` rows by severity including §2's unrecognised bucket, emitted only when a non-`PASS` row exists and omitted under `--compact` like `overlap_report` (`audit_merge.go:90-92`) -- and update §1's enumeration to five parts. Add a §5 test whose killing mutation is named (a counter that includes `PASS` rows, or one that survives `--compact`). Retitle Non-Goal 6 to what it now defers -- the `--record`/`--status` counterpart and its four pins -- so the section title and the item title agree.

finding: The doc repair this round names the claims correctly and then points their acceptance at a test that contains nothing of the kind, so the most expensive bytes in the release still have no failing arm. §4's second-guard paragraph ends: "This release updates both, and §5 test 3's doc assertions are over that sentence and `SKILL.md:145`'s `--status --check` clause". §5 test 3 is "**The two surfaces v0.31.1 exists for.** `tp config --extract` emits the field and `tp validate --project` accepts and rejects it" -- it has no doc assertion. Measured over the whole of §5 (lines 268-311): the substrings `SKILL`, `REFERENCE`, `docs_contract` and even `doc` occur zero times, so none of the eleven tests reaches `skills/tp/` at all. Two consequences. (1) The release changes at least four documented claims and no test forces any of them: the literal pinned at `docs_contract_test.go:96` (verified present as a `const`, and verified live in `SKILL.md`); the `--status --check` clause; `SKILL.md:152-153`'s "tp has no audit-side equivalent of `review_converge_on` yet", which shipping the field falsifies and which this spec still names nowhere; and the two five-name escalation tables §2 itself counts, `REFERENCE.md:347` and `SKILL.md:247` (both verified rendering exactly `skip-gate, raise-review-cap, raise-audit-cap, import-force, other`), which test 10 does not reach because it asserts the refusal's recorded decision, not the tables an agent reads. (2) The citation is off and hides that the two "claims" are one line: `SKILL.md:145` is the `--resolve` step; both the `docs_contract` literal and the `--status --check` clause sit together in the single sentence at `SKILL.md:149`. A stale sentence in `skills/tp/` is one wrong decision per agent per session -- the only cost in this release that recurs without bound -- and it is the one surface the spec leaves unasserted.
suggestion: Give §5 a doc test of its own rather than annexing test 3: assert that `SKILL.md:149`'s sentence no longer claims audit convergence counts every non-`PASS` row unconditionally, that `SKILL.md:152-153` stops saying no audit equivalent exists while still saying the role-scoping divergence is open (Non-Goal 1), and that `REFERENCE.md:347` and `SKILL.md:247` both render six decision names. Its killing mutation is the shipped `docs_contract_test.go:96` literal left in place. Then correct §4's citation from `SKILL.md:145` to `SKILL.md:149` and say the two claims are one sentence.

Four of those eleven spans were written or extended this round, in §1, §2, §2.2 and §4. §2's span is the one that states the case against itself: "it is recorded here as provenance, not as scope, because a scope sentence already satisfied cannot fail as acceptance." That is the correct test and it disqualifies the thirteen lines that follow it -- an implementer reading §2's opening paragraph for what to build gets one buildable sentence (the field, two values, task override > project config > built-in, the hint machinery) and then twelve lines on a sweep already done, which two shipped specs keep a wrong copy that must not be edited, that `TP_RUNNER_SEAM` and `notify_cmd` are exceptions to a precedence rule this field does not use, and a note about how to scope a grep so it does not match the sentence doing the scoping. Concretely -- §2's opening paragraph reduces to the field, its two values, its precedence and its hint, plus the one sentence that stops the five-layer chain being re-copied; §1's "This paragraph described the two-deliverable release for one round after the cut" goes (the paragraph is now correct, and the Overview is the highest-traffic text in the file); §2.2, §4's four parenthetical corrections and §5's preamble each keep their result and drop which draft was wrong. §3 was filed separately in round 6.

finding: §2.2 is a numbered subsection, 16 lines, whose second half establishes that its own subject does not exist for this release: "those 67 rows are read by no predicate this release adds", the live risk is forward-looking instead, "across v0.33.0-v0.36.0 there are **zero** out-of-enum severities in 238 non-`PASS` rows", and test 7 uses a legacy row "because it is convenient and real, not because the case is live". Its whole operative content is one clause already entailed by §2's fail-closed rule: legacy rows count as blocking, so no migration, no rewrite, no sink validation. A heading is not free prose in tp, and this is measurable rather than stylistic: `tp review` renders the section outline into every role prompt -- my own round-7 prompt lists "2.2 The 67 legacy rows" as a focus item and instructs me to apply my lens to it -- so an inert subsection is bought into five prompts per round for every remaining round, and each role spends its attention discovering there is nothing there. The same signal reaches the decomposer, which reads headings to size the task list and finds a named population of 67 rows in fifteen round files with no task attached to it, and reaches `--diff-from`, which reports §2.2 as a changed section when only its null result was reworded (it was reported MODIFIED to me this round while its line count did not change). The section is also the only place §2's own justification is restated in a second, different form -- §2 grounds the fail-closed rule on v0.31.0 §4.1, §2.2 re-grounds it on a forward-looking corpus argument -- so a reader who takes §2.2 as the reason gets a reason the release does not depend on.
suggestion: Delete the subsection and put its result in §2 beside the fail-closed rule as one sentence: "Sixty-seven non-`PASS` rows recorded across v0.29.0-v0.32.0 carry `high`/`medium`/`low`; the fail-closed rule counts them as blocking, so nothing migrates and nothing is validated at the sink -- and they are not why the rule exists, since `ReviewRound.Clean` is stamped at record time and no predicate this release adds reads them." Keep the corpus counts where they are load-bearing -- test 7's note that all 67 carry a present, non-null severity, which is why it needs three fixtures.

finding: Four findings formed and dropped after checking them against the tree or against the argument, recorded per this round's instruction. (1) I was about to file this round's new paragraph "**The fence is on the field, not on the direction.** Both `=blocking` and `=all` are refused" as unearned strictness -- `=all` is the shipped default and the cap fence deliberately refuses only a raise, so refusing the safe direction looked like surface bought for nothing. It is the cheaper implementation, not the dearer one: a direction-scoped fence must parse and compare the value, a field-scoped one is the same predicate lookup the two shipped fences already use, and the paragraph's own argument holds -- a unit that can write `all` can write `blocking` on the next line. Dropped. (2) I was about to re-file round 6's `by_severity` request as unrepaired. It was repaired; what is wrong is where the repair was put, so I filed the placement instead.
